speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To narrow down the cause, have you noticed any recent fever, cough, or loss of appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That constellation of symptoms—especially the "B symptoms" of fever, night sweats, and significant weight loss alongside lymphadenopathy—is highly concerning. Have you noticed any skin rashes, joint pain, or changes in bowel habits like diarrhea or constipation? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the blood work; the elevated white blood cell count suggests an active infection or malignancy. Have you experienced any persistent cough, shortness of breath, or contact with someone recently diagnosed with tuberculosis? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis. Treat the trigger as decisive.
